title: WATCH-19 re-derivation: one of the two premises the nudge design leans on no longer holds, and the other is empirical rather than structural
function: §1 'Why the honeypot framing does not apply'
description: §1 claims the pot is 'by construction a fraction of the cost of the nudgeSize mints' and that 'there is no configuration of this mechanism under which claiming is profitable-in-isolation'. Neither is established by construction.
impact: No standalone loss. This is the AMPLIFIER that sets the ceiling on CLASS-002 and CLASS-003, and it removes the safety argument the design document leans on.
attackPath: 1. §1 claims the pot is 'by construction a fraction of the cost of the nudgeSize mints' and that 'there is no configuration of this mechanism under which claiming is profitable-in-isolation'.
2. Neither is established by construction. BatchNFTMinter.sol:57-59's 'by construction' is backed by NO code; executed counterexamples run at 9.5× and 20,000×.
3. Observed margin is ~6× (88 USDC pot vs ~518 USDS for 40 mints) — empirical, not structural.
4. A prolonged period of no batching (bots offline, gas spike, UI outage) lets the pot cross the profitability line with NO on-chain brake.
likelihood: low as a standalone event; certain as an amplifier of the two Mediums.
assumptions: None — this is a documentation-vs-code discrepancy verified from source.
justification: Low. No standalone loss and no independent attack path — the value impact is entirely accounted for in CLASS-002/CLASS-003, so raising this above Low would double-count. It is filed rather than folded silently into the existing suppressions because it IS the WATCH-19-nudge-law1-reopen-trigger firing on its own terms, and because suppressing a finding under the very lineage whose premises it falsifies is exactly the circularity Law 1 forbids.
recommendation: Rewrite §1 to state the margin as an OPERATIONAL invariant that must be monitored, not a structural one — or enforce it in code (cap the payout at a value-based fraction of what the batch actually paid).
